create_task.title: Create task
create_task.description: Create one task. It lands pending whatever status the caller asked for, and its id is server-minted. Send effort, the estimated effort: unknown, very_low, low, medium, high or very_high; it is unknown when none is sent and any other value is refused with 400. It is given its code, the next number in its project's series (SW193), unless the caller sends a code, which is kept; a code another issue of the project holds is refused with 409. Send files, the paths the issue will touch, as a list of strings (see taskmanager_task_patch); a task made without files reads an empty list. A person needs Can move on the backlog it lands in (the first backlog when none is named).

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.

list_tasks.title: List tasks
list_tasks.description: List the tasks matching the filter. Narrow by status, priority, run, the outside holder of blocked work (held_by), tag (repeat it to ask for tasks that carry every tag given), repo (the task's project_name), backlog (its id or name), step (the id or name of a step of that backlog, or of the first backlog when none is given) or untouched_days (not changed for more than that many days, 0 or more), and pass a limit (1 or more; 0 or less is refused with 400) unless you genuinely need the whole board. Tag, backlog and step match without regard to case. A task whose backlog is empty or no longer exists is in the first backlog, at the step its status names (or at no step). Also narrow by assignee (who holds it) or unassigned (true; not both), blocked, waiting and sinbin (true or false), has_todos (true or false), todos_open (true: at least one todo not Done), effort (unknown, very_low, low, medium, high or very_high), created_since and updated_since (RFC 3339, changed at or after), has_files (true or false: the files list is not empty or is), ids (repeat it, at most 100) and sort (rank, priority, updated or created; default rank). A bad value is refused with 400. A page holds at most 500 tasks in rank order: pass offset (0 or more) to read the next page of the same filter, until a page comes back short.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

list_overdue_tasks.title: List overdue tasks
list_overdue_tasks.description: List the open tasks whose due date passed more than the agency's overdue_grace_hours ago, the longest overdue first, each with how many whole hours it is overdue. as_of reads the board at another instant (RFC 3339); a scheduled routine opens follow-up work from this list.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

pending_tasks.title: What is pending
pending_tasks.description: The quick answer to what is pending, open or left, in one call: every issue that is not completed, failed or cancelled and that the caller can see. It returns total, by_step (the count at each step, in step order) and by_priority (critical, high, medium, low), counted over everything the filters match, and items: the first limit issues in rank order, each compact (id, code, title, state, backlog, step, priority, tags, rank, blocked) and without the description. Narrow by tag (repeat it to require every tag), backlog (id or name), step (id or name), priority, or q (words that must each appear in the title, the code or a tag, without regard to case). Also narrow by assignee (who holds it) or unassigned (true; not both), blocked, waiting and sinbin (true or false), has_todos (true or false), todos_open (true: at least one todo not Done), effort (unknown, very_low, low, medium, high or very_high), created_since and updated_since (RFC 3339, changed at or after), has_files (true or false: the files list is not empty or is), ids (repeat it, at most 100) and sort (rank, priority, updated or created; default rank). A bad value is refused with 400. limit defaults to 25 and is at most 100; pass offset (0 or more) to read the next page. Pass include_closed true and by_step also counts the issues of the same filters that are completed or cancelled, at their Done and Cancelled steps; total, by_priority and items stay the open issues. To read one issue in full use taskmanager_task_read; to page through every issue use taskmanager_task_list.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

next_ready.title: The next Ready issue to take
next_ready.description: Find the next issue a worker should take with one cheap call: the issues at the To do step that carry the Ready tag, lowest rank first. It returns total_ready (every Ready issue the filters match) and items: the first limit issues, each compact (id, code, title, priority, effort, tags, rank, backlog, step) and without the description. An issue tagged Sinbin, Blocked or Waiting is never returned, even if it also carries Ready. Narrow by backlog (id or name; a backlog the caller cannot see is refused as unknown) and tag (repeat it to require every tag). Also narrow by priority, repo (the issue's project_name), effort (unknown, very_low, low, medium, high or very_high), assignee or unassigned, has_todos, todos_open, has_files, created_since and updated_since (RFC 3339, at or after); a bad value is refused with 400. limit is 1 to 5 and defaults to 1. items is empty and total_ready is 0 when none match. To read the issue in full use taskmanager_task_read.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

pending_todos.title: What is left on the issues in progress
pending_todos.description: For one backlog, the todos that are not Done of every issue at its In Progress step, in one call, instead of reading the In Progress step and then each issue's todo list. backlog (its id or name) is required: a blank or missing one is refused with 400, and a backlog that does not exist or that the caller cannot see is refused as unknown, so its existence is not confirmed. An issue counts as in progress when it sits at the step named In Progress, without regard to case and whatever the step's id is (doing in Backlog, in-progress in the Municipal Journey Book); its status is ignored, and an issue at To do, Review, Done or any other step is never listed, so a backlog with no In Progress step lists nothing. For a smart backlog, the issues of the smart backlog that sit at an In Progress step of their own backlog. It returns total (the issues at the In Progress step), total_pending_todos (the todos that are not Done over all of them) and items: the first limit in-progress issues in rank order, each compact (id, code, title, priority, tags, step) with todos, the ones that are not Done in order, each with id, code, title, ordinality, state (To do, In progress or Blocked), blocked_reason and depends_on, and done and total, the counts taskmanager_task_todo_list_for_issue gives. An in-progress issue with no pending todo is still listed, with an empty todos list. limit defaults to 25 and is at most 100; pass offset (0 or more) to read the next page of issues. To read one issue's whole todo list use taskmanager_task_todo_list_for_issue.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the backlogs their groups can see.

timed_out.title: The issues in progress that are past their working-time cap
timed_out.description: For one backlog, the issues that sit at its In Progress step (the step whose name is In Progress, without regard to case; a card's status is ignored because step and status move independently) and whose time since their first worker Log entry is past their working-time cap (the issue's own, else the default, 15 minutes): the board's Time is up measure, in one call instead of reading every page of the In Progress step and each issue's Log. backlog (its id or name) is required: a blank or missing one is refused with 400, and a backlog that does not exist or that the caller cannot see is refused as unknown. An issue at that step with no worker Log entry at all is also returned. Each item has id, code, title, minutes_since_first_entry (null when there is no Log entry), cap_minutes, minutes_since_last_entry (null when there is no Log entry), clock_stopped (as taskmanager_task_caps_read reports it) and last_entry (kind, the first 200 characters of its text, created_at; null when there is none). It names no cause: whether the run was interrupted, idle or too big is the caller's call. Read-only: it moves and tags nothing.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the backlogs their groups can see.

find_tasks.title: Find issues by id, code or words
find_tasks.description: Find issues of the backlogs the caller can see by what the caller remembers of them. q is required and is one of: an issue id (a uuid, exact), an issue code such as SW39 or mun67 (exact or a prefix, without regard to case, the exact code first), or words, where every word must appear, without regard to case, in the title, the code, a tag or the description. A blank q is refused with 400. Open issues only unless include_closed is true. Narrow by backlog (id or name), step (id or name) and tag (repeat it to require every tag). It returns total, counted over everything that matches, and items: the first limit issues in rank order, each compact (id, code, title, state, backlog, step, priority, tags, rank, blocked, waiting, sinbin) and without the description, the same shape as taskmanager_task_pending. limit defaults to 25 and is at most 100; pass offset (0 or more) to read the next page. To read one issue in full use taskmanager_task_read.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

get_task.title: Read task
get_task.description: Read one task, its labels resolved.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The task to read.

update_task.title: Update task
update_task.description: Replace the mutable fields of one task. A status change is checked against the lifecycle, and moving from pending to in_progress is refused while anything still blocks it. The code is overwritten when a different one is sent and kept when none is sent, so it is never cleared; a code another issue of the project holds is refused with 409.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The task to update.

patch_task.title: Patch task
patch_task.description: Change only the fields you send and leave every other field of the issue as it is: tags, project, priority, effort (unknown, very_low, low, medium, high or very_high), rank, place and the rest. Use this to edit one field in one call. Sending tags replaces the whole tag list; an empty list clears it. files is the list of paths the issue will touch, so the hub can tell which issues in progress clash: each entry is a path relative to its repo, optionally prefixed with the repo name and a colon (hub-steward:code/app/src/app/menu/MenuEditForm.tsx), and a trailing slash means everything under that folder. At most 100 entries, each not blank, at most 300 characters, with no control character, no leading slash and no .. segment; duplicates and surrounding spaces are dropped; a bad entry is refused with 400 naming it. Sending files replaces the whole list and an empty list clears it; leaving files out keeps it. taskmanager_task_read returns it, an empty list when the issue has none. A status change is checked against the lifecycle. To move an issue between steps use taskmanager_task_move_to_step. A changed priority puts the issue at the top of its new priority group in its step and adds a Log entry such as Priority medium to high.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The task to patch.

add_task_note.title: Add a note to an issue's Log
add_task_note.description: Add one dated entry to the Log of an issue. Anyone who can see the issue may add one, a reader who cannot move it included. The writer and the time are set by the hub; nothing already in the Log is changed. kind is person (the default) or a worker; links are the commit, file, drawing or CI run the entry is about.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; recorded as the entry's writer.
The issue whose Log it goes in.
person or worker. person when left out.
A line or a longer write-up.
Links to the work, as a list of strings.

list_task_notes.title: List the Log of an issue
list_task_notes.description: List the entries in the Log of one issue, oldest first: writer, kind, text, links and time. Send nothing else for the whole Log. To read only what was added since you last looked, pass after, the id of the last entry you saw (or an RFC 3339 time): only strictly newer entries come back, and an id that is not an entry of this issue is refused with 400. kind (person, worker or automatic; repeat it for several) keeps only entries of those kinds: automatic is what the hub wrote itself, worker is what a worker wrote. limit (1 to 200) keeps the newest that many entries, still oldest first. They combine: after, then kind, then limit.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The issue.

get_task_caps.title: Read the caps and consumption of an issue
get_task_caps.description: Read, in one call, the three caps a worker runs under on this issue (input tokens, output tokens and runtime seconds), the default for all workers, the issue's own numbers when it has any, and what the current or last run has used with whether the runtime clock is stopped because the worker waits for the owner's answer. Runtime is working time. used is absent when no worker has run.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The issue.

get_caps_nearest.title: Read the nearest cap of many issues
get_caps_nearest.description: For a list of issues (task_id, repeated) or every issue of a backlog (backlog, id or name; at most 500, in rank order) return, in one call, each issue's caps in force (its own numbers, else the default) and nearest: the cap its last or current run is closest to, with key (input_tokens, output_tokens or runtime_seconds), used, cap and ratio (used over cap, above 1 once past the cap). nearest is absent when no worker has run on the issue. started_at is the time of the issue's first worker or person Log entry, when it has one, never the hub's own automatic notes, so a screen can work out the time left of a running issue. interrupted is true when the hub stopped the clock because no usage write arrived for the idle limit; a screen then says Interrupted, not Time is up. An id that does not exist or that the caller cannot see is left out. Send task_id or backlog, at most 500 ids. To read one issue's caps and consumption in full use taskmanager_task_caps_read.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

set_task_caps.title: Give an issue its own caps
set_task_caps.description: Give one issue its own cap numbers, which replace the default for that issue; a cap not sent keeps its current value, or the default if the issue had none. Each number is a whole number of at least 1: input_tokens, output_tokens, runtime_seconds (working time). Returns the caps in force and the consumption.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The issue.

clear_task_caps.title: Use the default caps on an issue
clear_task_caps.description: Remove the issue's own cap numbers so the default for all workers applies again. Returns the caps in force and the consumption.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The issue.

write_task_usage.title: Write what a worker has used on an issue
write_task_usage.description: Called by the runner while a worker runs: replace the consumption of the issue's current run with the totals so far, input_tokens, output_tokens, seconds_used (working time), clock_stopped (true from the worker's question to the owner until the answer) and, when the runner knows them, files_uncommitted (the files the worker changed that are not committed; an empty list means none). Zeros start a new run. The hub sets the time it was written. When no usage write arrives for worker_idle_stop_seconds (default 600) on an issue In Progress, the hub stops the clock itself (clock_stopped and idle_stopped, one automatic Log entry saying why) without moving the issue or tagging it Sinbin, and the next write restarts the clock. When any total reaches a cap in force (the runtime cap is not applied while the clock is stopped) the hub itself stops the worker's issue if it is In Progress: it adds one worker Log entry (the cap passed, the three figures against their caps, the last step finished, what is left, the files not committed), drops Ready, Waiting and Blocked, adds Sinbin and moves the issue to To do. The reply says stop: true with the passed caps; the runner then ends its session. Returns the caps in force, the consumption, stop and passed.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The issue.

get_worker_caps_default.title: Read the default caps for all workers
get_worker_caps_default.description: The three numbers every worker runs under on an issue that carries none of its own: input_tokens 500,000, output_tokens 100,000 and runtime_seconds 900 until changed.

set_worker_caps_default.title: Set the default caps for all workers
set_worker_caps_default.description: Change the default caps; send any of input_tokens, output_tokens, runtime_seconds (each a whole number of at least 1) and the rest stay. Only the Product owner group may. Returns the default now in force.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session.

add_task_reference.title: Add a reference to an issue
add_task_reference.description: Say what an issue is about: one file, folder, issue, screen or tool, or website link. Anyone who can see the issue may add one, a reader who cannot move it included. A file or folder is a repo and a path on the repo's main branch; an issue is its number; a screen or tool is its name; a link is an http or https URL. The writer and the time are set by the hub, and an entry a person adds is confirmed. The same thing twice on one issue is refused.

args.description: Who is adding it, from the session; recorded with the entry.
The issue it is about.
file, folder, issue, screen or link.
The repo, for a file or folder.
The path inside the repo, the issue number, the tool or screen name, or the URL.

propose_task_reference.title: Propose a reference for an issue
propose_task_reference.description: The assistant's way to say what an issue seems to be about, from searching: one file, folder, issue, screen or tool, or website link, in the same form as adding one. It is saved unconfirmed and shown as the assistant's until a person confirms it or removes it. Anyone who can see the issue may propose. The same thing twice on one issue is refused.

args.description: Who is proposing it, from the session; recorded with the entry.
The issue it seems to be about.
file, folder, issue, screen or link.
The repo, for a file or folder.
The path inside the repo, the issue number, the tool or screen name, or the URL.

confirm_task_reference.title: Confirm a proposed reference
confirm_task_reference.description: A person agrees that a proposed reference is right. It stays marked as the assistant's and is no longer waiting. Confirming one already confirmed changes nothing. Anyone who can see the issue may confirm.

args.description: Who is confirming it, from the session.
The issue.
The reference to confirm, from the list.

list_task_references.title: List what an issue is about
list_task_references.description: List the references of one issue, oldest first: kind, repo, target, who named it (person or assistant), whether a person has confirmed it, who added it and when. Whether a file or folder is still on the repo is not checked here.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The issue.

remove_task_reference.title: Remove a reference from an issue
remove_task_reference.description: Take one reference off an issue; this is also how a file that was renamed or deleted is fixed, by removing it and adding the right one. Anyone who can see the issue may remove one.

args.description: Who is removing it, from the session.
The issue.
The reference to remove, from the list.

list_task_states.title: List task states
list_task_states.description: List the agency's task states in order, each with the lifecycle statuses it covers, so a board can draw one column per state.

move_task_to_state.title: Move task to state
move_task_to_state.description: Move one task into a named state. The task walks the shortest legal path of lifecycle statuses into that state; a task already in it is left alone, and a state it cannot reach is refused with the reason.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The task to move.
The name of the state to move it into, as the agency's task states list it.

list_backlogs.title: List backlogs
list_backlogs.description: List the backlogs the caller can see, in order, each with its steps in order and the number of issues in the backlog and at each step, so a board can draw one column per step. A person sees a backlog only when one of their groups has access to it.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.

create_backlog.title: Create backlog
create_backlog.description: Add a backlog with a name and either its steps in order or rules. With steps it is a workflow: the name must not belong to another backlog and at least one step is needed. With rules (a match of all or any, and a list of rules each with a field, an operator and a value) it is a smart backlog: it holds no issues of its own and lists whatever the rules match, and the same rules cannot be saved twice (refused with the existing backlog's id and name).

args.description: The new backlog's name.
The names of its steps, in order; leave out for a smart backlog.
For a smart backlog: {match: all or any, rules: [{field, operator, value}]}; leave out for a backlog with steps.

set_backlog_rules.title: Set a smart backlog's rules
set_backlog_rules.description: Replace the rules of a smart backlog. The same rules as another smart backlog are refused with that backlog's id and name.

args.description: The smart backlog.
{match: all or any, rules: [{field, operator, value}]}.

count_backlog_rules.title: Count what rules match
count_backlog_rules.description: Say how many issues the caller can see that the given rules match, without saving anything, so the rules screen can show a live count.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
{match: all or any, rules: [{field, operator, value}]}.

rename_backlog.title: Rename backlog
rename_backlog.description: Give a backlog another name. Its steps and issues stay as they are.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
The backlog to rename.
The new name.

archive_backlog.title: Archive backlog
archive_backlog.description: Mark a whole backlog archived so the Backlogs list hides it. Its issues, codes and tags stay as they are and its issues still open by link; smart backlogs still read them. The first backlog cannot be archived.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
The backlog to archive.

unarchive_backlog.title: Unarchive backlog
unarchive_backlog.description: Bring an archived backlog back onto the Backlogs list.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
The backlog to bring back.

delete_backlog.title: Delete backlog
delete_backlog.description: Delete a backlog. A backlog that holds issues cannot be deleted; move the issues out first.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
The backlog to delete.

replace_backlogs.title: Replace backlogs
replace_backlogs.description: Set the whole list of backlogs and their steps in one call, as the app's edit screens do. A step or a backlog that holds issues cannot be left out of the list. A backlog is archived only when it carries archived true.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
Every backlog with its id, name and steps in order.

add_backlog_step.title: Add backlog step
add_backlog_step.description: Add a step to a backlog, directly after the step named in after, or last when after is left out.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
The backlog to add the step to.
The new step's name.
The id of the step it goes after.

rename_backlog_step.title: Rename backlog step
rename_backlog_step.description: Give a step of a backlog another name. The issues at it stay there.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
The backlog the step belongs to.
The step to rename.
The new name.

remove_backlog_step.title: Remove backlog step
remove_backlog_step.description: Remove a step from a backlog. A step that holds issues cannot be removed; move the issues out first.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
The backlog the step belongs to.
The step to remove.

reorder_backlog_steps.title: Reorder backlog steps
reorder_backlog_steps.description: Put the steps of a backlog in a new order. Name every step of the backlog once.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session.
The backlog to reorder.
The ids of its steps, in the new order.

move_task_to_step.title: Move task to step
move_task_to_step.description: Put one issue at a step of a backlog. Name the backlog and the step by id; moving to another backlog is done by naming a step of that backlog. The caller needs Can move on the backlog it goes to.

args.description: Who is moving it, from the session.
The issue to move.
The id of the backlog.
The id of the step in that backlog.

claim_task.title: Take an issue
claim_task.description: Take one issue in a single atomic call: move it to the In Progress step of its backlog (the step that holds the In Progress status, else the step called In Progress or Doing) with status in_progress, write the first Log entry (kind worker, "Taken by <caller>. Caps in force: <input> input, <output> output, <minutes> minutes"), and return the issue compact (id, code, title, status, priority, effort, tags, backlog, step), the id of that entry (note_id) and the caps in force (the issue's own, else the default). Refused with 409 and the reason when the issue is tagged Sinbin, Blocked or Waiting, waits on an open dependency, is already in progress or has left To do; when two callers claim at once exactly one succeeds and the other is told the issue is already in progress. Refused with 403 when the caller lacks Can move on the backlog; 404 when the issue is unknown or the caller cannot see it. The caller needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.

args.description: Who is taking it, from the session; recorded as the writer of the entry.
The issue to take.

claim_next.title: Take the next ready issue
claim_next.description: Pick and take the next issue a worker should do in one atomic call, so two agents never take the same one. It looks at the issues at the To do step that carry the Ready tag, lowest rank first, skips any tagged Sinbin, Blocked or Waiting, any that waits on an open dependency, and any whose files overlap an issue in progress (the rule of taskmanager_task_file_overlaps; an issue with no files overlaps nothing), and takes the first one left exactly as taskmanager_task_claim does: moves it to the In Progress step, writes the first Log entry and returns the issue compact, note_id and the caps in force. It also records the agent (default the caller) as the assignee and a lease: lease_until, lease_minutes from now (default 30, 1 to 240; 400 outside that). Narrow by backlog (id or name; one the caller cannot see is refused as unknown) and tag (repeat it to require every tag). Refused with 409 and no issue taken when none is free, 403 when issues are free but the caller lacks Can move on their backlogs. Before it looks, every issue still In Progress past its lease_until is put back at To do, its assignee cleared and a Log entry written saying the lease ran out. Keep the lease alive with taskmanager_task_heartbeat.

args.description: Who is taking it, from the session; recorded as the writer of the entry. A person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.

heartbeat.title: Renew the lease of an issue you took
heartbeat.description: Extend the lease of an issue an agent took with taskmanager_task_claim_next: lease_until becomes lease_minutes from now (default 30, 1 to 240; 400 outside that). agent (default the caller) must be the assignee the claim recorded. Refused with 409 when the issue is not in progress, was taken without a lease, is held by another agent, or its lease had already run out (every lease past its lease_until is released first, so the issue is back at To do and claimable again). 403 without Can move on the backlog, 404 when the issue is unknown or not seen. Nothing is written when it is refused. Returns id, code, agent and lease_until.

args.description: Who is renewing it, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The issue whose lease to renew.

release_task.title: Release an issue as Blocked or Sinbin
release_task.description: Stop work on an issue you took, in one call. mode is blocked (a problem a person must look at) or sinbin (you stopped at a cap and the owner reviews it). The hub writes the Log entry (kind worker, the mode, your reason and your links), tags the issue with the one mark and drops Ready, Waiting, Blocked and Sinbin so never two of them are left (every other tag is kept), sets the todo you name Blocked with the reason when mode is blocked, sets its status back to pending and moves the issue to To do. Refused with 409 unless the issue sits at the backlog's In Progress step (the step named In Progress without regard to case, or with the id doing or in-progress), whatever its status, 403 without Can move on the backlog, 400 for another mode, a blank reason or a todo that is not one of this issue's (or sent with mode sinbin), 404 for an issue or todo that is not found or not seen. Nothing is written when it is refused.

args.description: Who is releasing it, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The issue to release.

list_backlog_access.title: List who can use a backlog
list_backlog_access.description: List the groups that have access to a backlog and what each may do: Can see, Can move or Can edit. The Product owner group always has Can edit. Each group also says which agency roles it holds (roles), no_role when none of them lets its members read tasks (so they still see nothing), and role_too_small when the group has Can move but no role lets its members edit tasks (so they can only look).

args.description: The backlog to read.

give_backlog_access.title: Give a group access to a backlog

task_brief.title: Everything a worker reads before starting an issue
task_brief.description: Read an issue the way a worker starts on it, in one call instead of five: the issue in full (description included), caps as taskmanager_task_caps_read gives them (default, in_force, own and used), log (the last log_limit Log entries, oldest first, and every entry of kind person beyond them too, because a person note is an instruction), todos (the issue's todo list with done and total, as taskmanager_task_todo_list_for_issue gives them), depends_on (each issue this one waits on as {id, code, title, step, state, open, last_entries}, where open is true while that issue is not Done or Cancelled and last_entries are the last 3 Log entries of that issue, oldest first) and needed_by (each issue that waits on this one as {id, code, title, step, state, open}). An issue in a backlog the caller cannot see is not named or read: hidden_depends_on and hidden_needed_by carry how many were left out. log_limit is 1 to 50 and defaults to 10; a value outside that is refused with 400. An issue the caller cannot see is refused as not found. Read-only.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The issue to brief.

file_overlaps.title: The issues in progress that touch the same files
file_overlaps.description: Before taking an issue, learn which issues in progress touch the same files, so two agents do not edit one file at once. Send taskID (an issue whose files list is used) or files (a list of paths, repeat it for several, for when no issue exists yet), or both; one of the two is required, 400 otherwise, and a bad path is refused with 400 as taskmanager_task_patch refuses it. items are the issues in progress, in any backlog the caller can see (the step named In Progress, without regard to case; a card's status is ignored), whose files list overlaps, each with id, code, title, step and overlapping: the pairs {asked, theirs} of paths that overlap. Two paths overlap when they are equal, or one is a folder (a trailing slash) containing the other, within the same repo prefix. The issue asked about is never listed against itself, and an issue with an empty files list overlaps nothing. An issue in a backlog the caller cannot see is not listed or counted, and an issue the caller cannot see is refused as not found. Read-only.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

next_ready_batch.title: Several Ready issues that touch different files
next_ready_batch.description: Find the issues an orchestrator can start at the same time with one call: the issues at the To do step that carry the Ready tag, lowest rank first, chosen greedily so that the files of no two returned issues overlap and none overlaps an issue in progress. Two paths overlap when they are equal, or one is a folder (a trailing slash) containing the other, within the same repo prefix, as taskmanager_task_file_overlaps reads them. count is 1 to 10 and defaults to 3; anything else is refused with 400. items are the chosen issues, each compact (id, code, title, priority, effort, files) and without the description. skipped lists the candidates passed over because they clash, each with id, code, title and clashes_with, the code of the issue in progress or the earlier chosen issue it clashes with. An issue with no files is left out and counted in unfiled_left_out, unless include_unfiled is true, and then it clashes with nothing. An issue tagged Sinbin, Blocked or Waiting is never returned. Narrow by backlog (id or name; a backlog the caller cannot see is refused as unknown) and tag (repeat it to require every tag). Read-only: it claims and moves nothing.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

board_snapshot.title: The state of the board in one call
board_snapshot.description: Learn the state of the board in one call instead of reading pending, lists, overdue and dependencies. Narrow by backlog (id or name; a backlog the caller cannot see is refused as unknown) and stalled_days (default 2). It reads the open issues the caller can see and returns steps, one per step in step order, each {name, count, oldest_days, oldest_code} where count equals by_step of taskmanager_task_pending for the same backlog, and oldest_days is how many whole days the least recently changed issue of that step has gone without a change (a named backlog lists all its steps, zeros included; with none, only steps that hold an issue); agents, the issues In progress per assignee {agent, in_progress, codes}, most loaded first, with an empty agent for issues nobody holds; stalled, the issues In progress not changed for more than stalled_days {id, code, title, agent, days}, the longest first; blocked_chains, every issue tagged Blocked {id, code, title, waits_on}, where waits_on lists the open issues it depends on as {code, blocked}, blocked being true when that issue is itself Blocked, so a chain reads link by link; ready, the number of Ready issues at the To do step that are not Sinbin, Blocked or Waiting (the total_ready of taskmanager_task_next_ready); and todo_progress {done, total}, the todos over the issues In progress. A stalled_days below 0 is refused with 400. Read-only.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

changes_since.title: What changed on the board after a cursor
changes_since.description: Read what changed after a cursor, so an orchestrator need not re-read the board. Send no cursor to get no changes and a cursor that marks now; send the next_cursor of the last answer to read on. A cursor is opaque. changes are in time order, each with id, code, title of the issue, kind, from, to and at. Two kinds are readable from what the hub stores: created (the issue was filed; from and to are empty) and priority (from and to are the old and new priority, read from the Log entry a priority change writes). A move, a hand-over, a status or tag change and a delete are not reported, because nothing stored says when they happened. An issue the caller cannot see is not reported. Narrow by backlog (id or name; a backlog the caller cannot see is refused) and tag (repeat it to require every tag). limit defaults to 100 and is at most 500; a larger one and a cursor this call did not return are refused with 400. has_more is true when the page is full and more follow; when nothing new came back next_cursor is the one sent. Read-only.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

unblock_impact.title: Which open issues finishing would unblock the most others
unblock_impact.description: Rank the open issues by how many other open issues finishing them would unblock. An issue is listed when at least one open issue waits on it (a depends_on relationship). direct is the number of issues waiting on it, total the number down the whole chain (an issue reached by two paths is counted once, and a cycle does not loop), and dependents the codes of all of them. Completed, failed and cancelled issues are neither listed nor counted, and an issue the caller cannot see is not counted. Ordered by total, then direct, then rank. items are compact (id, code, title, step, priority, direct, total, dependents) and without the description. limit defaults to 10 and is at most 50; a larger one is refused with 400. Narrow the listed issues by backlog (id or name; a backlog the caller cannot see is refused as unknown) and tag (repeat it to require every tag). Read-only.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

lint.title: Which issues break the filing rules
lint.description: Check issues against the filing rules before an agent picks them up. Send taskID for one issue (404 when it does not exist or the caller cannot see it), or backlog and step (id or name, both optional) for the open issues there, in rank order. Each item is an issue (id, code, title) with its findings, each a rule and a short message; an issue that breaks nothing has an empty findings list. The rules are no_description, no_done_when (the description has no Done looks like, Pass when or Done when), no_todos, last_todo_not_documentation (the last todo's title does not say document), no_files, effort_unknown, no_priority and todo_without_description. total counts every issue that matches and clean counts the issues on this page with no findings. limit defaults to 50 and is at most 200; a larger one is refused with 400; pass offset (0 or more) for the next page. Read-only.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

task_dependencies.title: What an issue waits on and what waits on it
task_dependencies.description: See at once why an issue is Waiting, without reading each issue. depends_on lists the issues this one waits on and needed_by lists the issues that wait on it; each is {id, code, title, step, state, open}, where open is true while that issue is not Done or Cancelled, in rank order. blocks_start is true when any issue it waits on is open. An issue in a backlog the caller cannot see is not named: hidden_depends_on and hidden_needed_by carry how many were left out, and a hidden open one still makes blocks_start true. An issue the caller cannot see is refused as not found. Read-only.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The issue to read the dependencies of.

To do, In progress, Done or Blocked.

Each todo carries its id, code, title, instructions, ordinality, depends_on (the ids of the todos it waits on), status (the API value), state (To do, In progress, Done or Blocked; a failed todo reads Blocked) and blocked_reason. done and total count the issue's todos. An issue with no todos returns an empty list and 0 of 0.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The issue.

Read-only; an issue the caller cannot see is 404.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The issue.

todo_ready_board.title: The todos that can start now across the issues in progress
todo_ready_board.description: The todos that can start now, from every issue at the In Progress step of its backlog (the step named In Progress, without regard to case, whatever its id), in one call, so a worker that wants a piece of work does not read each issue first. A todo can start when it is not Done, not Blocked and every todo it waits on is Done, the same rule as taskmanager_task_todo_ready. items are ordered by the issue's rank, then the todo's order in its list; each carries the todo (id, code, title, instructions, ordinality, state, can_run_parallel) and its issue (issue_id, issue_code, issue_files). total counts every match, not only the items returned. Narrow by backlog (id or name; a backlog that does not exist or that the caller cannot see is refused as unknown) and tag (repeat it to require every tag on the issue). limit is 1 to 100 and defaults to 25; anything else is refused with 400. Read-only; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the backlogs their groups can see.

Read-only; an issue the caller cannot see is 404.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The issue.

The task to link.

link_todo_to_run.title: Link step to run
link_todo_to_run.description: Record that one step belongs to one run, so rolling the run back reaches it.

args.description: The run.
The step to link.

set_failure_budget.title: Set recovery budget
set_failure_budget.description: Say how many recovery activations one lineage is allowed. Meaningful on the root run.

args.description: The run whose budget to set.
How many activations are allowed.

increment_failure_budget.title: Charge recovery budget
increment_failure_budget.description: Charge one recovery activation against a lineage's budget and say what is left. Charging the same child twice is a no-op.

args.description: The top of the chain, which holds the budget.
The recovery run being charged.

rollback_workflow_run.title: Roll run back
rollback_workflow_run.description: Undo one run: move it to rolling_back, compensate what it produced, then finish it as rolled_back. A person needs Can move on the backlog the issue of the run is in.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue of the run is in.
The run to undo.
Why it is being undone.

delete_workflow_run_artifacts.title: Compensate run artifacts
delete_workflow_run_artifacts.description: Reset the tasks one run produced and soft-delete its steps. Refused while another run still depends on one of them.

args.description: The run whose artifacts to compensate.

cancel_workflow_run.title: Cancel run
cancel_workflow_run.description: Begin cancelling one run, giving in-flight work until the deadline to quiesce, and cancel every task it holds that has not finished. A person needs Can move on the backlog the issue of the run is in.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue of the run is in.
The run to cancel.
Why it is being cancelled.
Who issued the cancel, from the session.
When in-flight work must have stopped by, as an RFC 3339 string.

finalize_workflow_run_cancellation.title: Finish cancelling run
finalize_workflow_run_cancellation.description: Close out a run whose quiesce deadline has passed.

args.description: The run to close out.

touch_workflow_run_last_event_at.title: Mark run alive
touch_workflow_run_last_event_at.description: Record that an event touched one run, which is what keeps the watchdog off it.

args.description: The run touched.
When it was touched, as an RFC 3339 string.

mark_timeout_published.title: Mark timeout announced
mark_timeout_published.description: Record that a timeout was already announced for one run, so it is announced once.

args.description: The run announced.

handle_run_timeout.title: Handle run timeout
handle_run_timeout.description: Act on one run having gone quiet for too long.

args.description: The run that went quiet.

handle_task_timeout.title: Handle step timeout
handle_task_timeout.description: Act on one task or step having stalled inside a run.

args.description: The task or step that stalled.
The run it belongs to.

open_case.title: Open case
open_case.description: Open one case for the caller, about the subject the body names. Its id, status and timestamps are server-owned.

args.description: Who brought the request, from the session.

get_case.title: Read case
get_case.description: Read one case by its storage key.

args.description: The case to read.

list_cases.title: List cases
list_cases.description: List cases, newest opened first, narrowed by requester, subject or status when given.

open_sourced_tasks.title: Open tasks from a source
open_sourced_tasks.description: Open one dated task per item a source lists, all in one transaction: a source (an opaque reference the host passes, such as the raw key of what listed the items) and items, each with a title, an optional description, an RFC 3339 due time and an optional key (the title when absent). An item already opened from the same source opens nothing again, so a replay is safe; each item comes back with its task id and whether this call opened it.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the first backlog, where these issues land.

generate_tasks.title: Generate tasks over a list of subjects
generate_tasks.description: Create one task per subject key from one template, all in one transaction: a run (an opaque name the host gives this generation), a template (title, optional description, priority, RFC 3339 due time and estimated hours) and subjects, the opaque keys the host listed, such as the groups or register records a query returned. Each task carries its subject key as its linked_ref. A subject already generated under the same run creates nothing again, so a replay is safe. At most 5000 subjects in one call; a blank or repeated subject refuses the whole call.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the first backlog, where these issues land.

create_repeating_task.title: Create repeating task
create_repeating_task.description: Create one repeating task: a title, an optional description, a schedule and an actor or role assignee. The schedule is a start (RFC 3339), an optional end (RFC 3339), an IANA time zone and either an iCalendar rule or a list of YYYY-MM-DD dates. At each period's start a task is made, due by the period's end. Its id is server-minted.

get_repeating_task.title: Read repeating task
get_repeating_task.description: Read one repeating task: its schedule, its assignee and whether it is stopped.

args.description: The repeating task to read.

list_repeating_tasks.title: List repeating tasks
list_repeating_tasks.description: List repeating tasks, oldest first, narrowed by assignee kind and id when given.

stop_repeating_task.title: Stop repeating task
stop_repeating_task.description: Stop one repeating task. It makes no further tasks and every task it already made is kept. Stopping it again changes nothing.

args.description: The repeating task to stop.

link_case_task.title: Link task to case
link_case_task.description: Work one task for one open case. A task serves at most one case. A person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue is in.
The case.
The task.

list_case_tasks.title: List case tasks
list_case_tasks.description: List the tasks worked for one case.

args.description: Who is asking, from the session; a person sees only the issues of the backlogs their groups can see.
The case.

end_case.title: End case
end_case.description: End one open case by hand, done or cancelled, with a reply to its requester, even when it has no tasks. Cancelling also cancels its open tasks; done is refused while a task is still open. When it cancels the case, a person needs Can move on the backlog of every issue of the case.

args.description: Who is writing, from the session; a person needs Can move on the backlog the issue of the case is in.
The case to end.
done or cancelled.
What the requester is told.

vote_case.title: Vote on case
vote_case.description: Give one open case a member's vote. The vote counts for the caller, from the session, and the caller is recorded as who cast it. A member votes on a case once, however often it is cast. The requester already counts as the first vote. member_kind is member, or left out; owner or agent is refused. Returns the case with its votes.

args.description: The open case to vote on.
The member the vote counts for, from the session.
Who casts the vote, from the session.
What the voter is in the agency: member, owner or agent. Owners and agents are refused.

take_back_vote.title: Take back vote
take_back_vote.description: Take one member's vote off an open case. The requester's own vote, which counts as the first, stays. Returns the case with its votes.

args.description: The open case.
The member whose vote is taken back.

list_case_votes.title: List case votes
list_case_votes.description: List the votes stored on one case, oldest first: the member each counts for and who cast it. The requester's own vote counts without being stored, so it is not listed.

args.description: The case.

list_cases_by_votes.title: List cases by votes
list_cases_by_votes.description: List open cases, most votes first and the earlier opened first among equals, each with its vote count. Narrowed by requester, subject or status when given; status defaults to open.

list_my_cases.title: List my cases
list_my_cases.description: List the cases the caller opened, newest opened first, narrowed by subject or status when given.

args.description: Whose cases, from the session.
